story: Ezra Furman had released Perpetual Motion People in 2015 and played Pickathon in 2016 before returning in 2018. Transangelic Exodus came out February 9, 2018 on Bella Union, a concept record Furman called a half-true memoir, and Drowned in Sound found it quite brilliant. Twelve Nudes followed in 2019, All of Us Flames in 2022 and Goodbye Small Head in 2025.
artist_reel_line: Goodbye Small Head came in 2025, seven years after the Transangelic Exodus concept album.

intro: A Nashville fiddler and country singer.
story: Joshua Hedley is a fiddler from Naples, Florida, long a Nashville sideman nicknamed Mr. Jukebox at Robert's Western World. His debut, Mr. Jukebox, came out April 20, 2018 on Third Man Records, which signed him as only its second country artist after Margo Price, and Paste and American Songwriter both liked it. He played Pickathon that year. Neon Blue followed on New West in 2022, and All Hat, produced by Ray Benson of Asleep at the Wheel, in 2025.
artist_reel_line: All Hat, from 2025, was produced by Ray Benson.

story: Sam Blasucci and Clay Finch grew up in Glendale and La Cañada Flintridge near Los Angeles, met in a high school music class and began as a duo in coffee shops, rising through the Grateful Dead cover band Grateful Shred. Their self-titled debut came out October 6, 2017 on Spiritual Pajamas, and they played Pickathon in 2018. From Liberty Street, on Yep Roc in March 2020, was recorded at the Los Angeles house it is named for, Roscoe's Dream followed in 2022, and Swinging Stars in 2023. In 2026 Blasucci released two solo albums, Physical Dream and Black Rose.
artist_reel_line: Sam Blasucci released two solo albums in 2026.

story: The Blind Boys of Alabama began in 1939 in Talladega, among students at the Alabama Institute for the Negro Blind, and founding member Jimmy Carter still sings lead. The group has five Grammy Awards, plus a Lifetime Achievement award in 2009 and a National Heritage Fellowship, and joined the Alabama Music Hall of Fame in 2010. Almost Home, in 2017, carried Let My Mother Live, their tenth Grammy nomination, at the January 2018 awards. They played Pickathon that year and the closing ceremony of the 2022 World Games in Birmingham. Carter has said they began not for fame or awards, only to sing gospel and touch lives.
artist_reel_line: Jimmy Carter, a founding member, still sings lead; they played the 2022 World Games closing.

story: The Weather Station is the Toronto project of the singer-songwriter and former child actor Tamara Lindeman, active since 2006. The self-titled fourth album came out October 6, 2017 on Paradise of Bachelors and moved her toward a fuller band sound, and she played Pickathon in 2015 and again in 2018. Ignorance, on Fat Possum in February 2021, was shortlisted for the Polaris Music Prize, and Lindeman has said the title describes moving through denial into understanding. Humanhood, in 2025, earned a 2026 Juno nomination for Adult Alternative Album.
artist_reel_line: Humanhood earned a 2026 Juno nomination for Adult Alternative Album.

story: Alela Diane was born in Nevada City, California, in 1983, and Joanna Newsom, also from there, invited her to her first solo appearances before she moved to Portland. The Pirate's Gospel, self-released in 2004 and reissued by Holocene Music in 2006, took its title from a night of rowing a canoe across a dark lake, singing gospel songs with friends. NPR profiled her in 2009 around To Be Still. About Farewell came in 2013 and Cold Moon, with the guitarist Ryan Francesconi, in 2015, and Cusp in 2018 was the album in hand when she played Pickathon, after visits in 2007, 2009, 2011 and 2012. Looking Glass followed in 2022 and Who's Keeping Time? in 2026.
artist_reel_line: Looking Glass came in 2022, and Who's Keeping Time? in 2026.

intro: A Syrian-born songwriter in Los Angeles.
story: Azniv Korkejian was born in Aleppo, Syria, to Armenian parents, was raised in Saudi Arabia and settled in Los Angeles, where she worked as a film dialogue and music editor. After a show at The Echo she approached Matthew E. White, and her self-titled debut as Bedouine came out June 23, 2017 on his Spacebomb label, with arrangements by Trey Pollard; The Guardian's Kitty Empire called it elegant, honeyed country-soul. She played Pickathon in 2018. Bird Songs of a Killjoy followed in 2019 and Waysides in 2021, and her fourth album, Neon Summer Skin, came on Thirty Tigers in 2026.
artist_reel_line: Neon Summer Skin, her fourth album, came out on Thirty Tigers in 2026.

story: Haley Heynderickx was born in Stockton, California, in 1993 to a Filipino-American family, learned to sing in church while growing up in Forest Grove, Oregon, and graduated from Portland State. The Fish Eyes EP in January 2016 led to her debut, I Need to Start a Garden, on Mama Bird Recording Co. on March 2, 2018, and she took lines for it from a notebook where she keeps things people say at awkward moments. Pitchfork, The New York Times, Stereogum, Paste and NPR all praised it. She played Pickathon that year and returned in 2023 and 2025. Seed of a Seed came in November 2024 on Mama Bird, and What of Our Nature on Fat Possum in 2025.
artist_reel_line: What of Our Nature came out on Fat Possum in 2025.

intro: A Chicago poet and soul singer.
story: Jamila Woods is a poet from Chicago's far South Side whose first chapbook, The Truth About Dolls, came out in 2012. Her debut album, Heavn, arrived July 11, 2016 on SoundCloud and landed on year-end lists at NPR, Esquire, Consequence of Sound and Pitchfork, which ranked it 36th. She played Pickathon in 2018. LEGACY! LEGACY!, on Jagjaguwar on May 10, 2019, named every track for an artist of color, and Woods has said she wrote it looking through the lenses of the people she names, their work and their words. Water Made Us came in 2023 and You Are Spring! in 2026.
artist_reel_line: LEGACY! LEGACY! named every track for an artist of color; Water Made Us came in 2023.

story: Hana Elion and JJ Mitchell met in 2011 at Wesleyan University in Connecticut and became fast friends. As Overcoats they released a self-titled EP in 2015 and the debut album Young on April 21, 2017 on Arts & Crafts, and NPR's Bob Boilen counted it among the best albums of 2017. They played Pickathon in 2018. The Fight followed March 6, 2020 on Loma Vista, then Winner in 2023 and an EP, moved back to town, in 2026, all of it written together; they say there are no Hana songs or JJ songs, only Overcoats songs.
artist_reel_line: An EP, moved back to town, came out in 2026.
